bug_semantics: Unauthenticated user enumeration (CWE-204) on FormaLMS password recovery. POST to the public /lostpwd route (index.php?r=adm/homepage/lostpwd, action=lost_pwd, userid=...) looks up the username via HomepageAdm::sendLostPwd; unknown users return USER_NOT_FOUND and HomepageAdmController::lostPwd renders Lang::t('_INEXISTENT_USER','register') ('The username you've inserted doesn't exist. Please check and retry'), while a registered username triggers a reset mail and _MAIL_SEND_SUCCESSFUL_PWD. The same oracle exists for lost_user (email) and in the legacy UserManager::performLostpwdAction path. CVE-2026-26744 remains PUBLISHED (cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED; GHSA withdrawn_at=null).
flaw_origin: The oracle was first written in this public git history in 48ffe2139a82791878ce94a50aad8c9493c5ba3d (2013-07-08, 'initial revision from docebo CE 4.0.5', git-svn-id svn/trunk@6): UserManager::performLostpwdAction returns $lang->def('_INEXISTENT_USER') when getUser()/getUserByEmail fails, versus _MAIL_SEND_SUCCESSFUL(_PWD) when the account exists (html/lib/lib.usermanager.php). Immediate parent db08b4b6eca361fd02084961265cfc33c4e79d52 is the empty tree (4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904, 0 files), so the vulnerable lines are absent there. 7cd41aba25e88ab0c21ccf97491a144a4ae63c66 (2017-02-28) is a refactor that copied the same USER_NOT_FOUND vs SUCCESS_SEND_LOST_PWD split into HomepageAdm::{sendLostPwd,sendLostUserId} and HomepageAdmController::lostPwd under the new /lostpwd MVC route; 9bfa9de0fe2a9b83690a3d4fca917426edda43d0 only moved that switch earlier in lostPwd() for inline form errors. No finer public Docebo CE member is reconstructable (GitHub code search for performLostpwdAction in lib.usermanager.php returned 0; disconnected tag VER-D.4.0.5/9575c92b is the same blob but not an ancestor of master).

reasoning: CVE-2026-26744 is a real CWE-204 in FormaLMS password recovery: /lostpwd discloses whether a username exists by returning _INEXISTENT_USER for unknown ids and a mail-sent success page for registered ones. The live sink is HomepageAdmController::lostPwd plus HomepageAdm::sendLostPwd, but that pair is a 2017 MVC refactor of UserManager::performLostpwdAction, which already implemented the identical lookup-then-distinct-message oracle. Per protocol a refactor is not a BIC. The smallest surviving public git object that first wrote those vulnerable lines on the master lineage is 48ffe2139a82791878ce94a50aad8c9493c5ba3d (Docebo CE 4.0.5 import). Its parent is the empty tree, so parent-tree absence is directly verified. That import cannot be decomposed into finer public members. 48ffe213 is an ancestor of the 4.1.18 version bump and of HEAD 4.1.43. AI is judged only on the BIC commit object: human author/committer Claudio Anelli, git-svn trailer, no AI co-author or generator markers, so verdict is NOT_AI. No later commit genericizes the /lostpwd responses; 4.1.19+ still carry the oracle, so the finding is unpatched with fix_sha null.
remaining_gap: unpatched; no upstream fix SHA at research time (HEAD 4.1.43 still maps USER_NOT_FOUND to _INEXISTENT_USER on /lostpwd).

potential_fix.approach: In HomepageAdmController::lostPwd (and UserManager::performLostpwdAction), always render one generic message for both existing and unknown usernames/emails (e.g. 'If an account exists, a recovery email was sent'), send mail only when the lookup succeeds, and apply the same uniform response to action=lost_user. Optionally add a constant-time delay and rate limit.
potential_fix.rationale: A single response for valid and invalid identifiers removes the observable _INEXISTENT_USER vs _MAIL_SEND_SUCCESSFUL_PWD discrepancy that currently enumerates registered usernames on /lostpwd.
